issues.body: The writer leaves `last_ok` untouched on every absent/unparseable response while incrementing `fail_streak`, but the consumer rule says any record whose `last_ok` is older than the TTL reads as never-observed and admits. Therefore a bucket that was once well formed and then remains malformed will refuse only from streak N until `last_ok` expires; after one weekly window plus slack it becomes row 4 and admits forever even though this tick still has a shape failure and probes continue succeeding at the transport layer. This defeats the stated consecutive-drift gate precisely for long-lived provider shape drift and contradicts the claim that only a sustained probe outage decays toward admission.
issues.fix_hint: Track freshness of the observation/outcome separately from `last_ok` (for example, a last-probed or last-shape-failure timestamp), and define expiry so only genuinely unobserved/unprobed state decays to row 4. Continuous successfully received malformed responses must remain row 3 after the threshold. Add a named transition test where malformed responses continue beyond the TTL and a mutant that incorrectly reclassifies that state as never-observed/admitted.
issues.title: The TTL eventually converts continuous observed drift back into permanent admission

verdict.summary: The prior round's missing durable state machine and incomplete stale-comment inventory are now addressed, but the proposed freshness rule makes the new drift refusal self-disabling. Because this design record is intended to govern the later admission gate, that internal state-machine contradiction remains a major completeness defect.
